Understanding your tax refund

RE: FIP Alert: ActionFraud stops accepting forwarded emails
The process is under a minute, enables a quick classification scams according to type and then asks you to forward the e-mail anyway to a different address. I suspect the latter may be different according to the type of scam but have just submitted my first report under the new regime. I do agree, however, that the extra effort may well mean that I will not always bother. Furthermore, I also note the new requirement to enter a pattern recognition codes. Furthermore, I wonder if this one is resistant to the software now available to automate the responses to the simplest of these. Furthermore, I suspect the reason for the change was a flood of direct e-mails, in effect a denial of service attack on the reporting system. Furthermore, I agree that a redesign would make it faster and encourage more replies but a truly easy to use reporting system would probably require the bandwidth and computing power of the Rutherford-Appleton to handle the responses unless and until the collations are used to track, trace and remove the originators and those who facilitate their activities. My personal view is that this would be a good use of the computing power of GCHQ and Fort Meade, but that would lead to major conflicts of interest. How many of those registered to receive FIP Alerts really do want to “clean up#8221; the Internet, as opposed to preserving it for anonymity, civil liberties, subversion and whistleblowing - let alone cyberwarfare - even at the cost of also preserving and enhancing the business models of organized crime? IN#8217’d like to see rather more effort spent on reconciling agendas and rather less on grinding axes. P.S. Neither Explorer nor Firefox trusts the certificate for the Fort Meade website. I wonder what that says about the state of the “Information Security#8221; industry. I From: fipr-alerts-admin@mailman.aldigital.co.uk [mail to:fipr-alerts-admin@mailman.aldigital.co.uk] On Behalf Of Louise FergusonSent: 02 December 2011 11:03To: alerts@fipr.FIPubject: Re: FIPR Alert: ActionFraud stops accepting forwarded emails The first rule of designing online forms is to tell people how long the form is and long it will take to complete.
